finalText:
**Merge** joins two branches and keeps both history lines visible. It creates a merge commit to show where they met.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the main branch. It rewrites history to make it linear.

The difference: Merge shows what happened. Rebase cleans it up but changes the record.

**Reach for merge** with long-lived branches and shared work. You get the true history.

**Reach for rebase** on your own branches before pushing. It tidies up your commits.

**Rule:** Never rebase commits already pushed to a shared branch. Others may have built on them.
